items.name: ISO/IEC 23894
items.description: AI-specific risk-management guidance aligned with ISO 31000 — the methodology ISO 42001 clause 6 points to for running the four-stage risk process (identify, assess, treat, monitor) across an AI system's lifecycle.

requirements.text: Work out where the AI system could go wrong: involve the people who build, operate and are affected by it, fix the scope and risk criteria, and identify risks across the system's lifecycle.
requirements.rationale: Identification aligned with ISO 31000 general risk-management principles keeps the AI risk inventory grounded in who actually touches the system.

controls.description: Run lifecycle risk-identification workshops with builders, operators and affected-party representatives; record scope, criteria and resulting risks in the AI risk register.

requirements.text: Analyse and evaluate the identified AI risks — how likely they are and how severe their consequences could be — using established risk-assessment methods adapted to AI systems.
requirements.rationale: Assessment turns a risk list into a prioritised one; methods borrowed from general frameworks need adapting to AI-specific failure modes.

controls.description: Score each identified AI risk for likelihood and impact using a documented AI-adapted method; review the scoring with a second assessor.

requirements.text: Decide how to respond to each evaluated AI risk — avoid, mitigate, transfer or accept it — so the chosen treatment is deliberate and traceable back to the assessment.
requirements.rationale: Traceable treatment decisions prevent silent acceptance of AI risks nobody consciously took on.

controls.description: Record a treatment decision (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) with owner and rationale for every evaluated AI risk; link mitigations to the controls that implement them.

requirements.text: Keep watching AI risks throughout the system's lifecycle and review whether the treatments are working, feeding what you learn back into the risk process.
requirements.rationale: AI systems drift; monitoring closes the loop so the risk process stays current rather than a one-off exercise.

controls.description: Monitor treated AI risks against their treatment effectiveness on a scheduled cadence; report changes to management review and re-enter the identification stage when new risks emerge.
